Use the table of future values of \$1 to find the future value of \$3000 invested per year at $6\%$ p.a. for 4 years, with interest compounded every 6 months.

\extable{497_q24_t1}

solutions.latex:
Interest is compounded every 6 months for 4 years, so there are $8$ periods at $3\%$ per period; the table factor is $8.8923$.
$$\begin{aligned} FV &= 3000 \times 8.8923 \\ &= \$26\,676.90 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Uses the correct table value, or equivalent merit

The following table shows the future value of an annuity of \$1. Miriam is saving for a trip and estimates she will need \$15 000. She opens an account earning 3% per annum, compounded annually.

\exfigure{3306_q7_1}
How much does Miriam need to deposit every year if she wishes to have enough money for the trip in 4 years' time? Write your answer to the nearest dollar.
How much interest will Miriam earn on her investment over the 4 years?

solutions.latex:
The table gives the future value factor $4.184$ for 4 periods at $3\%$.
$$\begin{aligned} A \times 4.184 &= 15000 \\ A &= \dfrac{15000}{4.184} \\ &\approx \$3585 \text{ per year} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Writes the correct equation using $4.184$, or equivalent merit

6218.stem: Barry makes regular payments of \$2450 into his investment account at the end of every quarter and never withdraws any money from the account. His account accrues interest at a rate of 3.2% p.a. compounded quarterly.

figures.cap: fill-in table of time period, A_n and balance for A0 to A4

parts.latex: By converting the given rate, show calculations to determine how Barry's investment can be modelled by the recurrence relation $A_{n+1} = A_n(1.008) + 2450$.

Complete the balance of the savings account after 1 year in the table below.

\exfigure{3306_q9_1}
How much interest did Barry accrue over the 1-year period?
What is the balance of the savings account after 3 quarters?

solutions.latex:
Convert the annual rate to a quarterly rate.
$$\begin{aligned} r &= \dfrac{3.2\%}{4} \\ &= 0.8\% \end{aligned}$$
Each quarter the balance earns $0.8\%$ interest, so it is multiplied by $1.008$, and then the $\$2450$ payment is added at the end of the quarter. Starting from $A_0 = 0$:
$$\begin{aligned} A_1 &= 0(1.008) + 2450 = 2450 \\ A_2 &= 2450(1.008) + 2450 = 4919.60 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ A_{n+1} = A_n(1.008) + 2450$$
criteria: Converts the rate to $0.8\%$ per quarter, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
A table of future value interest factors for an annuity of \$1 is shown.

\exfigure{500_q12_1}

Simone deposits \$1000 into a savings account at the end of each year for 8 years. The interest rate for these 8 years is 0.75% per annum, compounded annually.

After the 8th deposit, Simone stops making deposits but leaves the money in the savings account. The money in her savings account then earns interest at 1.25% per annum, compounded annually, for a further two years.

Find the amount of money in Simone’s savings account at the end of ten years.

solutions.latex:
For the first 8 years use the annuity table factor for 8 periods at $0.75\%$, which is $8.2132$.
$$\begin{aligned} FV &= 1000\times 8.2132 \\ &= \$8213.20 \end{aligned}$$
Then compound this for 2 years at $1.25\%$ per annum.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= 8213.20\times(1.0125)^2 \\ &\approx \$8419.81 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the balance after 10 years is } \$8419.81$$
criteria: Finds the correct future value of the annuity and attempts to apply the compound interest formula, or equivalent merit
Identifies the correct interest factor from the table, or equivalent merit
